pattern.title: From generation capacity to power quality: AI’s new electrical frontier
pattern.before: The AI infrastructure race focused almost exclusively on securing enough megawatts, assuming that once connected, power delivery would be stable and predictable.
pattern.shift: Early signals indicate that AI workloads cause violent, sub‑second power draw fluctuations that physically stress on‑site equipment and inject instability into local grids.
pattern.now: The binding constraint is no longer just generation capacity, but the ability of data center electrical systems and utility networks to absorb volatile load profiles without failure.
pattern.conclusion: If verified, AI build‑out might be limited not by power plants but by grid‑stability margins, raising costs and narrowing the list of viable sites.

insight.title: AI’s power problem is no longer about size, but stability
insight.formula: AI workload volatility × low grid inertia = operational risk to equipment and supply
insight.explanation: As AI clusters toggle between idle and full utilization, they create frequency and voltage swings that conventional power systems cannot absorb, potentially leading to equipment damage and local outages.
